subject: URGENT: Customer queue starvation & 5xx surge — executive attention requested
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@crestpay.com>, CrestPay SRE <sre@crestpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: High queue depths / 5xx spike impacting CrestPay (reserved capacity shortfall)

Olivia / CrestPay SRE team — we're seeing sustained queue depth growth for your reserved pool in us-west-2 starting ~07:40 PDT. Symptoms: elevated P50->P95 latency, rising 5xx (~3.6% at peak), and task queueing that is bumping requests into fallback throttles. Attached is a short perf export (crestpay_perf_summary.csv).

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm any unusual traffic patterns / batch size changes on your side in the last hour?
- We need exec visibility — this is impacting a handful of high-value payment flows. Recommend a short bridge and temporary routing to our hosted fallback model while we stabilize.

Short mitigation notes we've started:
- Identified a hot KV-eviction path during long-context scoring (see flamegraph attached).
- Rolling a precautionary throttle on non-critical scoring route (will reduce throughput by ~12% but should cut queueing).

I'll loop engineering and ops now (Jonas/Hannah/Rishi) and prepare a one-page for execs. If this needs a rapid credit/procurement path for burst capacity, call it out here and I'll escalate.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0184

Attachments: crestpay_perf_summary.csv, kv_eviction_flamegraph.png

We need an ETA for stabilization. Can you confirm whether routing to hosted fallback will preserve our PII controls (we need an account-level exception)? Also loop in your procurement/contact for short-term burst/billing implications.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:02:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: High queue depths / 5xx spike impacting CrestPay (reserved capacity shortfall)

Quick internal read:
- Preliminary telemetry shows reserved pool consumption for CrestPay is at 112% of committed tokens over the last 30m; autoscaling didn't add capacity because the reservation ceiling was hit.
- Backpressure is cascading: long-context scoring keeps evicting KV and increasing per-token cost, which lengthens service time and pushes more requests into queue.

Immediate ops plan (30m window):
1) Route a small percentage (10-20%) of non-P0 traffic to our hosted model variant (same architecture, lower-cost instance). Need Lauren to confirm PII exception.
2) Apply the precautionary throttle on the scoring endpoint (Lauren noted, already queued).
3) Open a burst authorization: request +200 reserved units for 72 hours (sales/procurement follow-up).

I'll start the telemetry drill and coordinate the bridge. If exec escalation is required, prepare a one-pager with credit options and customer SLA risk.

Jonas
VP, Platform Ops
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:27:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: High queue depths / 5xx spike impacting CrestPay (reserved capacity shortfall)

Technical notes — quick triage:
- Root cause (prelim): KV cache eviction cycle + long-context scoring increases per-request kernel time. Not a GPU OOM — we're seeing kernel scheduling hot paths that increase latency variance.
- Short-term mitigations we can push now (under 30m):
  * Enable per-tenant KV pinning for CrestPay (reduces eviction churn, small memory bump).
  * Drop heavy post-processing on the scoring endpoint for the reconciliation job (reduces CPU/GPU overlap).
  * Limit concurrent scoring sessions per session token until pool stabilizes.

I've prepared a small diff (patch_throttle.diff) with the throttle and pin changes; QA is minimal but sufficient for a canary (will roll to 3 hosts then scale). If we need an immediate rollback plan, we can revert pinning and the throttle as a second step.

Rishi
Head of Inference Engineering
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Executive Team <execs@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@crestpay.com>, CrestPay SRE <sre@crestpay.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:04:12 -07:00
Subject: ESCALATION: CrestPay reserved-capacity shortfall — request for exec decision (credits / burst)

Execs — brief summary and decision needed:
- What happened: CrestPay's reserved pool hit its configured ceiling; long-context scoring caused KV churn and per-request times increased, producing queueing and elevated 5xx rates. Customer impact is visible (payment timeouts).
- Impact: customer-facing errors and retries; potential SLA exposure for top-of-funnel payment flows.
- Mitigations in flight: routing ~15% non-critical traffic to hosted fallback, enabling per-tenant KV pinning, and a precautionary throttle on scoring. Rishi will push a small canary in the next 20 minutes.

Decision points for leadership: 
1) Approve a 72-hour burst reservation for CrestPay (+200 units) to buy runway while optimizations take effect. We will bill per the burst policy and offer a discretionary credit if appropriate.
2) Approve an emergency customer credit offer (recommended: one week of token credit) to address SLA pain.

Links: hubspot deal and incident doc in thread metadata.

Asks: please reply with APPROVE/DECLINE for (1) and (2) or request a 20-min exec bridge.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Success
